FINAL ORDER OF APPROVAL
On June 10, 2026, the Office issued a Notice of Intent to Approve ("NOi") the application
for approval for authority for Cogent Bank to exercise trust powers. On June 11, 2026, the Office
received the Applicant's written waiver of the right to an administrative hearing concerning the
Office's intended action.
Accordingly, it is ORDERED:
1. The application is APPROVED, subject to satisfaction of the conditions contained
in the attached NOL
2. The Applicant must satisfy the conditions of approval specified in the attached NO I.
Until these conditions have been met, or if any interim development is deemed to warrant further
action by the Office, the Office reserves the right to alter, suspend, or withdraw approval.
DONE and ORDERED this 15* day of June, 2026, at Tallahassee, Leon County,
Florida.

Dear Ms. Rossa:
NOTICE IS HEREBY GIVEN pursuant to chapters 655,658,660 and sections 120.60 and 120.80,
Florida Statutes, that the Office of Financial Regulation ("Office") has considered the information
presented in the application by Cogent Bank, Orlando, Orange County, Florida ("Applicant" or "Bank")
for authority to exercise trust powers and intends to approve the application based upon the following:
FINDINGS OF FACT
(1) The application for authority to exercise trust powers by the Applicant was filed with the Office
on April 1, 2026.
(2) On or about May 12, 2026, the Applicant applied to the Federal Deposit Insurance Corporation
("FDIC") with its intent to exercise trust powers. The FDIC subsequently approved the
application on June 1, 2026.
(3) Notice of the application was published in the Florida Administrative Register on April 3, 2016.
No hearing was requested and none was held.
(4) The decision due date for the application is August 6, 2026.
(5) The Applicant is a state-chartered bank located at 420 South Orange Avenue, Suite 150,
Orlando, Orange County, Florida.
(6) The Board of Directors of the Bank passed a resolution on March 19, 2026, approving the
establishment of a Trust Department.
(7) The Applicant submitted Madelayne Cordero ("Ms. Cordero") as the proposed Senior Trust
Officer.
(8) The Office conducted a background investigation of Ms. Cordero. The Office discovered no
information to preclude Ms. Cordero from serving as Senior Trust Officer.

CONCLUSIONS OF LAW
(9) The general condition of the Bank is sufficient to support the proposed trust department.
(10) The earnings and earnings prospects of the Bank, including the earning prospects of the
proposed trust department, are sufficient to support the anticipated expenses and any
anticipated operating losses of the trust department during its formative or initial years.
( 11) The capital structure of the Bank is adequate to support the trust department.
(12) Ms. Cordero has, or will be supplied with, sufficient trust and related investment, financial, and
managerial experience, ability, and standing to operate the trust department.
(13) Provision has been made for the trust department to occupy suitable quarters at the location
specified in the application.
Having considered the application, the Office concludes that the application satisfies the criteria of
section 660.26, Florida Statues (2025). Consequently, the Office intends to approve the application
subject to the following conditions:
(]) That the FDIC does not rescind, suspend, or withdraw its approval of the application for trust
powers by the Applicant.
(2) That the Bank's Senior Trust Officer shall be Madelayne Cordero.
(3) That securities are deposited or pledged to the Chief Financial Officer as required by section
660.27, Florida Statues, prior to commencement of trust business.
(4) That stockholder approval is obtained for amendment to the Bank's Articles oflncorporation
providing for the operation of a general banking and trust business. Applicant shall submit to
the Office the original Amended Articles of Incorporation, duly executed, together with the
filing fee due to the Department of State under section 607 .0122, Florida Statutes.
(5) That blanket bond coverage includes operation of trust department and that trust errors and
omissions insurance have been obtained.
The Office will issue a conditional Final Order of Approval after the expiration of the 21-day period
contained in the Notice of Rights unless the Applicant elects to waive rights to a hearing by providing
written notification of such waiver to the Office. Before all the conditions specified above and other
reasonable requirements of the Office have been fulfilled, or if any interim development is deemed by the
Office to warrant such action, the Office retains the right to alter, suspend, or withdraw approval of the
indirect change in control of the Bank and the Trust Company. This approval shall expire six months
from the date of the Final Order, unless the Office has granted a request for an extension of time for good
cause shown.
In taking this action, the Office has relied on the representations and commitments made by the Applicant
in the application and all supplemental information submitted. Every effort should be made to meet these
representations and commitments. Please keep the Office advised of the steps being taken to comply with
the conditions imposed in this Notice.
If you have any questions, please contact the Office at (850) 410-9513.

In the event that a hearing is requested, all parties will have the right to be represented by counsel
or other qualified representative, to offer written and oral testimony, to call and cross-examine
witnesses, and to have subpoenas and subpoenas duces tecum issued on their behalf. Pursuant to
Section 120.573, Florida Statutes, you are advised that mediation of this matter is not available.
